headline: Recommended the 5 Roby Street subdivision with conditions; approved up to $2,500 for Buckmeadow brush hogging.
summary: The commission voted to recommend the 5 Roby Street proposal for 13 single family homes and one multifamily building, with conditions on wetland buffer placards, planting, and ground cover. It approved brush hogging at Buckmeadow for no more than $2,500, to be completed by the end of October. It also approved the September 2, 2026 minutes as amended.
decisions: Approved the September 2, 2026 minutes as amended. Motion carried.
Recommended the 5 Roby Street subdivision with stipulations, including wetland buffer placards and a December 2027 landscape completion deadline. Motion carried.
Approved brush hogging at Buckmeadow for no more than $2,500, with the project completed by the end of October. Motion carried.
Commissioner Widhu agreed to replace Commissioner Darby as the Conservation representative on the Greeley Park Advisory Board.

plain_text:
NASHUA CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
October 6, 2026 
 
A.  Call to order 
 
A regular meeting of the Nashua Conservation Commission was called 
to order on Wednesday, October 6, 2026 at 7:00 PM, 229 Main Street, 
City Hall. 
 
B.  Roll call  
 
Members present:  Sherry Dutzy, Chair 
                         Dick Widhu, Vice Chair 
Carol Sarno 
 Will Darby (7:02pm)  
                         Gloria McCarthy  
                         Brandon Pierotti  
 
                         Amanda Griffith (Absent) 
                         Dale Carruth (Absent)  
                          
 
Also, in Attendance:    Levent Akinci, Sustainability Planner.
      
C.  Approval of minutes  
 
September 2, 2026 
MOTION to approve minutes as amended by Commissioner Sarno. 
Seconded by Commissioner Pierotti 
MOTION CARRIED 
D.  Old Business: 
Eric Newman, 5 Roby Street. Proposal to redevelop two parcels 
into a subdivision for 13 single family homes and one 
multifamily building with temporary impact to approximately 
1,300 SF of the wetland buffer for a prime wetland. Map 126. Lot 
23. Zone R-A – Urban Residence. Ward 6. 
Mark West, wetland scientist, led a discussion on a revised 
restoration and planting plan. The revised plan expands the 
planting area from the original 500 sq. ft (50x10) to 960 sq. ft 
(12x80) doubling the area. The width was adjusted to 12 feet wide

based on the commission’s request. Trees include: two native red 
maples to replace mature trees and mitigate impacts. Native shrubs 
planted 8-foot on center spacing (plus extra plants). 
• Clethra alnifolia (sweet pepperbush): spreads via rhizomes, 
serves as a strong pollinator. 
• Silky dogwood: produces food and flowers 
• Winterberry: food producer 
• Highbush blueberry 
 
Erosion control: Seed mix sourced from New England Wetland 
Plants to stabilize the buffer area and slopes. Along with straw 
mulching on all disturbed soil. Buffer area is not expanding 
further toward the wetland buffer edge; it is extended back 
towards the existing garage/home footprint. The one existing 
tree in the project area will have its tree well extended. 
 
• A full assessment from Lee Gilman has not yet occurred as he 
was unavailable to visit before the meeting. 
 
Fill and Grading Details: The area to be raised is limited to 
approximately 45 to 55 sq. ft, raised about 2.5 to 3 feet in 
height. Total additional fill required will be approximately 
10 to 15 yards to finish the yard level without extending the 
slope beyond its current limits. Wood chips will serve as ground 
cover on top of tarps. 
 
Invasive Species Management: Japanese knotweed, abandoned 
initial plan of deep burial due to concerns that it requires 
up to 16 feet of burial depth to stop resurgence. Replaced with 
the tarp smothering method and waterway-safe herbicide (Ranger 
Pro) on slopes where tarps are not feasible (e.g., above the 
asbestos disposal area).  
 
Commissioner Sarno recommended cutting burning bush to stumps 
and covering them with “buckthorn baggies” (or heavy-duty 
contractor bags fastened with zip ties acting like a mini 
tarp/umbrella) for 1-2 years to prevent stump sprouting without 
chemicals.  
 
Commissioner Dutzy made a motion for a favorable recommendation 
with the following stipulations: 
• Wetland Buffer placards placed every 50 feet along the 
wetland buffer boundary (e.g., on 4x4 posts, rocks, or tree), 
mounted using the guidance from Planning department.  
• Full execution of the landscape plan presented by Mark West, 
with a completion deadline set for December 2027.

• Ground cover must be wood chips over tarps as specified. 
 
Seconded by Commissioner Sarno 
 
MOTION CARRIES  
 
E. New Business: 
 
NONE 
 
F. NCC Correspondence and Communications 
 
BUCKMEADOW MAINTENANCE AND INVASIVE CONTRACTOR: 
 
Commissioner Sarno spoke about the brush hogging maintenance quote 
received by Miguel. Miguel came in at $2,100 to brush hog half 
the meadow this year, and $2,100 for the other half next year. 
Miguel will have to rent specialized equipment for this task. 
 
Commissioner Dutzy advised she was provided information that 
Knotts Land Care preforms brush hogging and would provide a quote 
as well. 
 
DISCUSSION ENSUED ON QUOTES AND FINANCES AND GETTING A SECOND 
QUOTE 
 
Commissioner Sarno made a motion to not exceed $2,500 and the 
project completed by the end of October. 
 
Seconded by: Commissioner Darby 
 
MOTION CARRIES 
 
DISCUSSION ENSUED REGARDING NON-DISCLOSURE OF THE APPROVED CEILING 
($2,500) UNTIL THE VENDER QUOTE IS RECEIVED. STAFF NOTED DRAFT 
MINUTES MUST BE POSTED WITHIN 5 DAYS. 
 
Commissioner Darby requested an update on available balances and 
interest accruals in the Conservation account. 
 
Levent Akinci agreed to coordinate with Deb Chisholm to provide 
updated balances. 
 
 
G. Commissioners Discussion

POTENTIAL ACQUISITION OF PARCEL H635: 
 
Commissioner Widhu was contacted via email by The Society for the 
Protection of New Hampshire Forests inquiring about the potential 
to purchase parcel H635. The forest society originally bought the 
parcel with the intention of selling it to Pennichuck Water Works. 
The parcel sits within the 150-foot watershed protection zone and 
is contiguous with city-owned/Pennichuck owned conservation land. 
A woods logging road runs through it, but it is split by wetlands 
and largely undevelopable. The Forest Society had previously 
proposed selective logging on the parcel, but abandoned the effort 
when the commission requested an official forest management plan.  
 
It was determined that Levent Akinci will reach out to the Forest 
Society to clarify their expectations regarding price or potential 
donation.   
 
 
111 MAIN DUNSTABLE ROAD: 
 
Discussion stemmed from an ongoing violation where an estimated 
98 trees were unlawfully clear-cut within the wetland buffer to 
expand a lawn. Trees and stumps where ground down and removed, 
making direct diameter-at-breast-height (DBH) field measurements 
impossible. Tree counts where derived from historic aerial 
imagery. Brandon Quigley’s report identified several white pines 
and other species, though multiple trees were classified as 
“unknown”. Estimated that the total lost DBH could exceed 1,000 
inches.  
 
Commissioner Sarno presented the Standardized Council of Tree and 
Landscape Appraisers (CTLA) formula used to calculate replacement 
value for mature trees. Variables include DBH, cost of the largest 
commercially available replacement tree (typically 3-4-inch 
caliper) species rating, location on the property, and pre-removal 
tree condition. Current city ordinance (NRO 190-117) provides for 
equivalent DBH replacement (either by equal caliper or multiple 
smaller trees adding up to the total removed DBH) and carries per-
day fines for non-compliance.   
 
Commissioner Sarno to distribute the CTLA valuation formula link 
to the commission. Levent Akinci to resend Brendan Quigley’s tree 
survey report and check existing legal provisions with City legal. 
Commission to evaluate consulting UNH Extension Forester Mike 
Gagnon for an uncompensated site review.
NCC 
September 2, 2026 
Page 5  
 
VOLUNTEER PROJECT AND COMMUNITY CLEANUPS: 
 
Commissioners discussed, Bishop Guertin Day of Service scheduled 
for November 5th at 9:30am. 
Commissioner Sarno proposed location focus on clearing bittersweet 
vines near the boardwalk end at Buckmeadow (following up on 
earlier teacher volunteer work), or alternative trail work along 
the river bike trail. Final site to be confirmed at the November 
4th meeting.   
 
Commissioner Dutzy discussed Joyce Park and the discover of 
illegal dumping of construction and demolition debris (including 
windows) down the embankment behind 131 Burke Street (parking lot 
of a contracting business). A conversation was had at this visit 
with (2) First Student bus drivers whom have observed unauthorized 
vehicles dumping trash after dark. There is also a similar dumping 
situation over at the Nashua River Boat ramp. It has been referred 
to City Code Enforcement. 
 
  
19 VISTA WAY ZBA APPROVAL: 
 
Commissioner Dutzy lead a discussion on attending the ZBA meeting 
for 19 Vista Way and the request that was approved by the ZBA to 
remove 21 trees within the conservation buffer. Commissioner Dutzy 
has expressed her extreme dismay and has written a draft letter 
to Community Planning for them to review to express her concerns 
to the ZBA. She finds that it is so egregious that if there is no 
change made to the decision she will resign from the Conservation 
Commission. Commissioner Dutzy had suggested topping the trees at 
15 feet to remove structural fall risk while preserving habitat 
trunks, rather than full removal. The ZBA condition stipulates 
that felled tree trunks/logs and debris must remain on-site in 
the woods. Cutting window allowed between November 1 st and April 
30th.  Commissioner Dutzy expressed city legal president (State 
Supreme Court ruling regarding a case with the Hooksett 
Conservation Commission in 2007) bars Conservation Commissions 
from appealing ZBA decisions because Conservations serve purely 
as advisory boards. Levent Akinci to review the HOA approval 
letter language with the City legal department to determine if 
the lake of dual approval invalidates the HOA sign-off or permits 
an appeal.

GREELEY PARK ADVISORY BOARD: 
 
Commissioner Darby reported scheduling barriers attending

Conservation
